differences.what: Message adds a framing, not present in the write-up, that the negative result 'extends Raman's "hold-vs-mention failed"' finding to a wider class of content/mode contrasts
differences.message_quote: That extends Raman's "hold-vs-mention failed" to a much wider class.

differences.what: Write-up explicitly credits Raman et al. 2026 for the random-direction control methodology used to show direction-specificity; the message reports the same 0.069 result without attributing the control design to Raman
differences.message_quote: Random direction of matched norm at the same dose: 0.069 (below baseline) — the gain is direction-specific.
differences.writeup_quote: a seeded random direction of matched per-layer norm at the same dose lands at 0.069 — below baseline, not just null — so the model is sensitive to this direction specifically, not to any large push (cf. Raman et al. 2026's random control).

message_source_quote: the only thing I could get to work is an engagement-stance direction at L20–24** — the same mechanism as Raman et al.'s white-bear steering (WBS, in `papers/`)
writeup_source_quote: I do not claim this is a wholly new mechanism: it is an engagement-stance vector applied at the concept-allocation zone, and WBS is the prior art for exactly that.
rationale: Both documents explicitly name Raman et al. 2026's white-bear steering (WBS) as the prior art whose family the method's engagement-stance direction belongs to, and both make essentially the same novelty claim: the specific imagery+global-clearing contrast and the negative result across six content/mode contrasts are the genuine contributions, while the mechanism itself is not new. The message adds one unsupported extension (linking to a specific 'hold-vs-mention failed' Raman result) not found in the write-up, and omits the write-up's explicit attribution of the random-control methodology to Raman, but these are minor and the overall level of credit and novelty framing is equal between the two.
